owner: Roblox High School Control Tower / Content QA
goal: Drive the canonical school UI toward the authorized RHS2 visual reference while keeping functional, visual, device, and runtime evidence separate. This document records only visible evidence and bounded implementation rules; it does not invent hidden asset IDs, remotes, catalog data, or server semantics.

keyFrames.purpose: Travel modal with compact HUD retained
job result modal with compact HUD retained

visualSystem.evidenceBoundary: Color values below are compression-tolerant implementation targets sampled from visible frames, not claims of original hidden RGB constants.

rhsBlue.use: primary panel headers / major blue surfaces

tabBlue.use: inactive tab and secondary blue controls

typography.rule: Replace generic Arial-heavy presentation with the closest Roblox built-in rounded/modern bold sans treatment consistent with the reference. Prefer Gotham/GothamBold/GothamMedium where available. Preserve exact verified strings when a text fixture exists.
typography.title: bold white, high contrast
typography.labels: bold/semibold white over dark or colored strips
typography.body: dark text on white result surfaces; white text on navy/blue feature surfaces

surfaceLanguage: Dark navy base panels with saturated royal-blue header bands.
Rounded rectangular controls with restrained corner radius, light outline/highlight, and stronger colored active states.
Compact edge HUD stays visually separate from world center.
Large feature panels use layered sections/tabs rather than a generic pale-blue card.

geometry.placement: status top-right immediately left/above the right rail; action rail right edge; shortcuts bottom center

requiredVisuals: Top-right status is a compact dark stack, not a pale school-day card.
Visible reference stack contains a thin weather/day/time row, a coin-style row, a gem-style row, and a purple level/progress strip.
Right action rail shows four large glossy rounded tiles: Shop red, Avatar cyan, House green, Travel gold.
Below the four large rail entries, the reference shows smaller colorful utility tiles; until exact semantics/assets are verified, use inert/reference-only placeholders rather than inventing actions.
Bottom quick bar shows four separated glossy rounded slots with cyan/dark/green/pink families and visible item art in the reference.
dataRules: Clock/day may use Foundation-owned school clock values already available to the client.
Do not label progression points as coins or invent gem balances without an authoritative server value.
Do not invent weather state. Hide/neutralize unowned data rather than fabricate live values.
Unknown icon asset IDs remain explicit evidence gaps.

visualContract: Large dark-navy modal offset toward center-left while compact edge HUD remains visible.
Bright royal-blue header band with white 'Travel' title and angled/right-ended visual treatment.
Circular/outlined close control in the top-right of the modal.
Two-tab row immediately below header; active tab gold/yellow, inactive tab deep blue.
Destination area is a multi-column image-card grid; cards use dark/blue framing and a black/dark label strip with centered white text.
Background gameplay remains visible around the panel.
travelModal.authorityRule: Only server-approved destinations may be interactive. Additional observed tiles can be visually represented only when their asset/destination authority is verified.

visualContract: Viewport-dominant state replaces/occludes the ordinary free-roam right rail.
Left preview stage remains visible with a large royal-blue 'Select an Item' callout and lower instructional text.
Right side uses bright blue shop chrome with title/subtitle, All/Vehicles/Skins tabs, search, sort, detail area and card grid.
Vehicle grid cards use saturated cyan/blue backgrounds, vehicle image, name and price/status footer.
Balances appear in two large blue strips along the bottom of the shop area.
Close control is a white outlined circle on dark navy.
dealership.authorityRule: Preview/search/sort/card selection are presentation. Purchase/ownership/spawn remain server-authoritative.

visualContract: Centered medium modal leaves compact status, rail and quick bar visible.
Header is vivid purple with subtle dotted/bubble texture; white title at left, white back/close controls at right.
Main body is white.
Job name/performance hierarchy uses dark bold type.
Performance meter is a rounded grey track with bright gold fill and orange result caption.
Earnings row separates coin amount and purple XP amount.
Level/progress strip uses dark outer track and vivid purple fill.
Primary dismissal is a centered bright green rounded button with white OK text.

visualStates.freeRoam: world-dominant; only compact edge HUD and quick slots visible
visualStates.dominantFeature: dealership family may replace ordinary rail while active
visualStates.closed: closing/dismissing any modal deterministically restores the same compact HUD state

nextProductSlice.activation: Only after the current vehicle-card repair is fully reconciled through exact-canonical push CI, Integration, Smoke rebind, and Control Tower releases the sole product slot.
boundedScope: Add one shared RHS2 visual-style helper/module.
Restyle persistent status, main action rail and quick slots to the locked visual contract.
Restyle Travel/Shop shell chrome to the locked navy/blue/gold treatment while preserving current authority semantics.
Add screenshot-independent static contracts for font family, palette family, surface hierarchy, modal close affordance, HUD retention and no-large-panel free-roam state.
Do not invent missing icon asset IDs, destination IDs, balances, weather, gems, catalogs, or hidden UI hierarchy.

acceptance: Static UI contract rejects regression to the pale LEGACY_PANEL/Arial look for the primary RHS2 surfaces.
Free roam has no large central permanent panel.
Status/action/quick placement remains responsive and safe on desktop 909x483, iPhone 852x393 and iPad 1024x768.
Travel retains status/rail/quick around the modal; dealership remains allowed to be viewport-dominant.
Rendered comparison at comparable FOV is still required before claiming exact RHS2 visual parity.
